prompt:
Create a 3x1 sprite sheet for a modern 16-bit-style pixel-art RPG: one MONSTER in three battle poses.

Image 1 is a LAYOUT GUIDE: three cells on white. In each cell the light-grey box shows where the monster stands and how big it is, the grey line is the ground, and the arrow shows the facing: the monster faces RIGHT, toward the heroes. Draw the SAME monster once in every cell, filling its box. Never draw the grey box, line or arrow.

Image 2 is the HOUSE STYLE: an approved hero sprite sheet from this same game. Match its sprite-pixel size, black outlines, flat shading with 2-3 tones per colour and level of detail exactly, but do NOT copy the hero; it is a different character.

Image 3 is an APPROVED MONSTER sheet from this same game (a DIFFERENT monster, idle | attack | hurt): match its sprite-pixel size, rendering, shading, outline weight and level of detail, and how much the poses move. Do NOT copy that monster's body, colours or equipment.

Render as true pixel art: the monster about 56-72 pixels tall in sprite pixels, every sprite pixel a hard-edged square, no anti-aliasing, no gradients.

Monster: a stocky deep-bodied river fish seen from the side, a tall rounded body covered in rows of hard rust-orange and dark bronze scales, a thick bony bronze plate over the head, a heavy jutting lower jaw with the mouth closed, a yellow eye, spiky dorsal and lower fins, a ragged forked tail; it hovers horizontally, nothing touches the ground, no water drawn; in every cell it floats in the upper part of its box with clear empty space below it, centred in its own cell. Keep every detail identical in every cell. FACE: its yellow eye under the bony head plate and the heavy jutting lower jaw are readable.

Cells:
- left cell: idle, a ready battle stance facing right.
- middle cell: attack, darting forward toward the heroes, the heavy lower jaw dropped open, the body level and horizontal, the head well inside the middle cell, facing right.
- right cell: hurt, knocked back, the body bent into a gentle curve while staying horizontal, the jaw closed, the spiky fins flattened, recoiling away from the heroes (leaning left), still facing right.

MOVEMENT: the attack and hurt cells are dramatic ACTION frames, not static stances. Keep the fish level and horizontal in every cell. The idle cell shows it at its lowest; in the attack and the hurt it rises a little, with more empty space below it: in the attack it darts forward to the right; in the hurt it is knocked back to the left with the body bent into a gentle curve; it always hovers, nothing touches the ground; the fins and the tail move with the motion. Each of the three silhouettes must be clearly different. BODY: in every cell, hovering above the ground as if swimming, nothing touches the ground, no shadow, no water, no splashes. No mist, smoke or ground effects.

One monster per cell and nothing else: no props on the ground, no effects outside the monster, no text.
Background: solid flat magenta (#FF00FF) everywhere, no floor, no shadows, no borders.
Avoid: two creatures in one cell, different creatures in different cells, background scenery, floor tiles, shadows on the ground, magic effects outside the cell, text, frame, border, grid lines, blurry, soft shading, gradient, 3d render, water, bubbles, splashes, motion lines, streaks, silver scales, green scales, red colour, legs, a vertical body, an eyeball body.
